text.p: Joe Carter, Jose Cruz Jr and Shawn Green all homered and drove in two runs to lead the Toronto Blue Jays to a 6-3 victory over the Cleveland Indians Wednesday.

After Carter homered in the fifth to give Toronto a 3-2 lead, Cruz, playing in his first home game as a Blue Jay, connected in the seventh for the go-ahead run. He also threw out the potential tying run at the plate in the eighth.
Ed Sprague had a pair of doubles for the Blue Jays, who have won consecutive games after collecting just one victory in their previous 10 contests.

Pat Hentgen (12-7) went seven innings, allowing three runs and 11 hits, for his third straight victory. Kelvim Escobar got his seventh save in as many chances, despite issuing three walks in the ninth.

"Tonight was a game. I hung in and battled," Hentgen said. "And Jose Cruz was huge. That's something, to hit a home run like that and then throw a guy out. He's special. The ball just jumps off his bat."

Albie Lopez (3-5) took the loss in relief, surrendering three runs and three hits, including two homers, over three innings. The Indians lost even though every member of the lineup reached base at least once. The Blue Jays turned five double plays for the second time this season.

At Minnesota, emergency starter Tim Wakefield threw seven strong innings on two days' rest and Jeff Frye and Scott Hatteberg drove in two runs apiece as the Boston Red Sox stopped the Twins 5-2 for their third straight victory.

Wakefield (6-13), starting for the injured Steve Avery, allowed two runs and seven hits, walking none and striking out seven. The knuckleballer threw 111 pitches two days after pitching eight innings in a 5-2 loss to Kansas City.
"I didn't have a problem doing it," said Wakefield. "I've done it in the past. When Avery got hurt yesterday, I immediately went to pitching coach Joe Kerrigan and said I can throw tomorrow."
The Red Sox have won eight of their last 11 games.
Rich Robertson (7-10), winless since June 14, gave up five runs in seven innings for his seventh straight loss.
In Seattle, Brady Anderson launched a solo homer with one out in the top of the 11th as the Baltimore Orioles edged the Mariners 4-3 for a split of their two-game series.

Jesse Orosco (4-3) got the final out of the 10th for the victory, retiring pinch-hitter Mike Blowers on a groundout with runners on first and second. Randy Myers pitched a 1-2-3 11th for his 32nd save in 33 opportunities.
Heathcliff Slocumb (0-6) took the loss.

Baltimore lengthened its lead in the American League East to 5 1/2 games over the second-place Yankees. The Mariners had their three-game winning streak snapped and dropped one game behind first-place Anaheim in the A.L. West.
In Anaheim, Jack Howell's two-run double snapped a sixth-inning tie and Tony Phillips added a homer and two RBI as the Angels defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 8-6.

Allen Watson (10-6) allowed four runs -- two earned -- and seven hits over 6 2/3 innings to become the third Angel pitcher to reach double figures in victories this season, joining Jason Dickson and Chuck Finley.
The Angels have won nine of their last 11 games. The Brewers have lost four of five following a season-high nine-game winning streak.
At Texas, Will Clark and Mike Simms each drove in a pair of runs as the Rangers won for just the second time in nine games, defeating the New York Yankees, 6-2.
Darren Oliver (8-10) got his fifth win in his last six decisions.

Andy Pettitte (13-7), a Texas native, allowed five runs and nine hits in seven-plus innings and fell to 4-3 lifetime against the Rangers. He lost for the second time in three starts following a four-game winning streak.
In Kansas City, Jose Rosado survived seven rocky innings to post his first win in more than seven weeks and Jay Bell hit a solo homer as the Royals edged the Detroit Tigers 5-4.
Rosado (8-8) snapped a personal five-game losing streak and won for the first time in nine starts. Jeff Montgomery, who has retired 30 consecutive batters, got his seventh save.
Bell's 19th homer gave him 72 RBI this season, a career high and the most by a Royal since Gary Gaetti had 96 in 1995.

In Oakland, Rafael Bournigal's two-out single in the bottom of the seventh scored Scott Brosius with the go-ahead run as the Athletics broke a year-long losing streak to the Chicago White Sox with a 3-2 victory.
T.J. Mathews (2-1), acquired six days ago from Baltimore, notched the victory with 1 1/3 hitless innings. Billy Taylor tossed a scoreless ninth for his 20th save.
The win snapped Oakland's nine-game losing streak to Chicago, dating back to July 31, 1996.
White Sox left fielder Albert Belle, mired in a 12-for-80 slump, went 0-for-4 and stranded eight runners.
